tools.name: ripgrep
tools.summary: Exact symbol and text search across tracked trees.
tools.why: Fast, ignore-aware, and sufficient for targeted context. `eng impact` uses it for reference discovery.
tools.failure_mode: Finds text, not meaning: misses dynamic references, macros and generated code.

tools.name: git grep
tools.summary: Search tracked files without extra tooling.
tools.why: Portable fallback when ripgrep is unavailable; matches the exact revision in Git.
tools.failure_mode: Same textual limits as ripgrep; untracked files are invisible to it.

tools.name: Language servers
tools.summary: Compiler-backed definitions, references and diagnostics.
tools.why: The most reliable symbol lookup when the language server is configured. Use it before text search for ambiguous symbols.
tools.failure_mode: Only as good as the project's build configuration; a stale index or failing build gives wrong answers.

tools.name: Cargo metadata
tools.summary: Build graph, package names and targets without reading the tree.
tools.why: The authoritative Rust workspace graph; safer than directory guesses.
tools.failure_mode: Describes the declared graph, not feature-gated or build-script-generated code paths.

tools.name: ast-grep
tools.summary: Structural search and rewrite across many languages.
tools.why: Useful when text search cannot distinguish a definition from a call site. Not adopted until false negatives are measured on real changes.
tools.failure_mode: Rules match syntax, not types; a pattern can silently miss variants.

tools.name: tree-sitter
tools.summary: Incremental parsing for structural indexes.
tools.why: A foundation for symbol extraction, but adds grammars and build surface. Current impact analysis is explicitly textual.
tools.failure_mode: Grammars lag language releases; parse errors degrade to partial trees.

tools.name: SCIP / LSIF
tools.summary: Persistent code-intelligence indexes for large repositories.
tools.why: Would improve cross-repository navigation; not justified until a repository's text search is measurably insufficient.
tools.failure_mode: Indexes go stale between builds; a stale index reports outdated references.

tools.name: cargo test / nextest
tools.summary: Rust unit, integration and doc tests.
tools.why: Native, deterministic and already the merge condition in Rust repositories.
tools.failure_mode: Proves only what the tests assert; feature flags and targets not built are not tested.

tools.name: pytest
tools.summary: Python unit and integration tests.
tools.why: Native framework with fixtures and parametrization; used only when the repository declares it.
tools.failure_mode: Fixtures and monkeypatching can hide real integration failures.

tools.name: node:test / Vitest
tools.summary: JavaScript and TypeScript tests.
tools.why: Prefer the framework already declared by the repository; do not add a second runner.
tools.failure_mode: Mocks and test environments (jsdom) differ from real runtimes.

tools.name: swift test
tools.summary: Swift package tests on macOS and Linux.
tools.why: Native SwiftPM test runner; required for Swift packages.
tools.failure_mode: Simulator and host differ from devices; UI behaviour needs separate tests.

tools.name: Gradle test
tools.summary: JVM and Android unit/instrumentation tests.
tools.why: Authoritative for Gradle projects; instrumentation tests need a device or emulator.
tools.failure_mode: Robolectric and emulators differ from devices; instrumentation tests can be flaky.

tools.name: Property-based testing (proptest)
tools.summary: Generate inputs from invariants instead of enumerating examples.
tools.why: High value for parsers, math kernels and state machines. Add per repository with a shrinking corpus and a deterministic seed.
tools.failure_mode: Generators can miss the interesting region; an unpinned seed makes failures hard to reproduce.

tools.name: Fuzzing (cargo-fuzz)
tools.summary: Coverage-guided input exploration for parsers and binary formats.
tools.why: Needed for hostile input surfaces. Requires a corpus, a crash triage process and a time budget; not a default fast check.
tools.failure_mode: Finds only what the harness reaches; no crashes in a short run is weak evidence.

tools.name: Mutation testing (cargo-mutants)
tools.summary: Test the tests by mutating production code.
tools.why: Useful evidence that a test suite detects faults; expensive and language-specific, so run it on critical modules rather than every commit.
tools.failure_mode: Slow, and surviving equivalent mutants create noise; easy to misread as a coverage score.

tools.name: Golden and snapshot tests (insta)
tools.summary: Freeze serialized output, CLI text, rendering and formats.
tools.why: Strong contract evidence when the golden files are reviewed and regenerated deliberately, never to make a red test green.
tools.failure_mode: Regenerating goldens to make a red test green turns them into rubber stamps.

tools.name: Contract and differential tests
tools.summary: Old/new fixtures and reference implementations for compatibility.
tools.why: Required for public APIs, schemas, persistence and protocols. A contract claim without a fixture is an opinion.
tools.failure_mode: Fixtures cover the cases someone thought of; real consumers may rely on others.

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.summary: Secret scanning for tracked files and history.
tools.why: High-signal maintained rules. The kit scans a hard-linked tracked tree, so build output is never scanned.
tools.failure_mode: Pattern-based: misses novel secret formats and flags fake ones; untracked files are not scanned.

tools.name: Semgrep CE
tools.summary: Language-aware SAST with a small, tested rule set.
tools.why: Runs locally and in CI, supports custom rules and fixtures. Eight baseline rules cover command injection, TLS, YAML, pickle and execSync.
tools.failure_mode: Only the rules configured; a clean run means those rules found nothing.

tools.name: OSV-Scanner
tools.summary: Dependency vulnerabilities from lockfiles.
tools.why: Uses OSV data, requires no account and works with Cargo.lock and other ecosystems. Findings are never suppressed to make a gate green.
tools.failure_mode: Needs network and a supported lockfile; advisories lag disclosure.

tools.name: actionlint
tools.summary: GitHub Actions syntax, expression and shell checks.
tools.why: Catches workflow mistakes before merge and works on every workflow file.
tools.failure_mode: Checks syntax and shell, not whether a workflow is safe to run on untrusted input.

tools.name: zizmor
tools.summary: Security audit for GitHub Actions workflows.
tools.why: Finds template injection, credential persistence and unpinned actions. The platform and kit run it as a gate.
tools.failure_mode: Static audit of workflow files; cannot see repository settings or secrets scoping.

tools.name: CodeQL
tools.summary: Deep dataflow and semantic code analysis.
tools.why: Strong for scheduled deep analysis, but heavier and GitHub-hosted. Semgrep remains the fast local gate; add CodeQL where its dataflow adds measured value.
tools.failure_mode: Slow and heavy; query coverage varies by language, and alerts need triage.

tools.name: Trivy / Grype / Syft
tools.summary: Image, filesystem, SBOM and vulnerability scanning.
tools.why: Adopt when a release produces container images or archives. The current pilot has no such artifact.
tools.failure_mode: Database freshness and noise; image scans miss what is fetched at runtime.

tools.name: Cosign
tools.summary: Sign and verify release artifacts and attestations.
tools.why: Only useful once there is an artifact and a signing policy. `release-check` can verify a supplied signature; it does not create keys or sign.
tools.failure_mode: A signature proves who signed, not that the artifact is safe; key or identity mistakes break trust.

tools.name: Git worktrees
tools.summary: One checkout and branch per independent unit.
tools.why: Native isolation with no extra service. The eng CLI records ownership and a concurrency cap.
tools.failure_mode: Isolate files, not shared caches, ports, databases or devices.

tools.name: eng CLI
tools.summary: Detect, impact, verify, guard, security, worktrees and evidence.
tools.why: A dependency-free control plane that gives humans, agents and CI the same answers.
tools.failure_mode: Runs what the config says; a weak config gives a green gate that proves little.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.summary: Shared, immutable quality gates and evidence artifacts.
tools.why: The existing CI system. Add a verify step to it; do not replace working pipelines. Pin every action to a commit SHA.
tools.failure_mode: A pull request runs its own copy of the workflow, so CI cannot vouch for changes to CI.

tools.name: Containers
tools.summary: Ephemeral, reproducible execution where native setup is insufficient.
tools.why: Useful for cross-platform builds and hostile fixtures. Do not add a container runtime when a local process is adequate.
tools.failure_mode: Image drift and unpinned bases break reproducibility; containers are not a strong security boundary on their own.

tools.name: sccache (S3-compatible)
tools.summary: Shared compiler cache for Rust (and C/C++) across runners, on S3-compatible storage.
tools.why: High value for large Rust workspaces. Only main-branch CI gets write credentials; PR builds and agents read. Separate prefixes per project and toolchain; never put credentials in the repository.
tools.install: cargo install sccache (or a pinned CI action)
tools.failure_mode: A poisoned or mismatched cache returns wrong artifacts; key mismatches (paths, flags, toolchain) give near-zero hit rates.

tools.name: Evidence records
tools.summary: Hash-chained JSON for every verification run.
tools.why: The audit unit. Records commands, exit codes, durations, output hashes, Git state and scanner versions; skipped is never pass.
tools.failure_mode: Local and unsigned: proves integrity of the chain, not who produced it.

tools.name: CI artifacts
tools.summary: Retain evidence outside the agent's context.
tools.why: CI uploads `.agents/evidence/` even when the gate fails, so a reviewer can inspect the failing log after the runner is gone.
tools.failure_mode: Retention expires; artifacts are only as trustworthy as the job that uploaded them.

tools.name: OpenTelemetry
tools.summary: Traces, metrics and logs across agents and services.
tools.why: Adopt when there is a collector and a consumer for the data. Evidence JSON is the current audit unit.
tools.failure_mode: Instrumentation without a consumer is cost without value; traces can leak sensitive data.

tools.name: Agent evaluation harness
tools.summary: Scored tasks in isolated worktrees.
tools.why: Measures pass rate, duration and diff size for any agent command. The stub validates the harness; a no-op agent must score zero.
tools.failure_mode: Two smoke tasks: detects gross regressions, not model quality.

tools.name: AGENTS.md
tools.summary: The repository's authoritative policy and map.
tools.why: One place for commands, invariants, compatibility, security and evidence rules. Skills do not duplicate it.
tools.failure_mode: Stale policy misleads agents; it is guidance, not enforcement.

tools.name: Agent Skills
tools.summary: Seventeen task-specific entrypoints with workflows and completion criteria.
tools.why: Load one skill for the task instead of injecting every instruction into every context.
tools.failure_mode: Text, not enforcement: an agent can ignore a skill; the gate still has to catch it.

tools.name: ADRs and architecture docs
tools.summary: Durable decisions linked to source and tests.
tools.why: Prevents stale chat summaries from overriding current code. Invalidate docs when the code they describe changes.
tools.failure_mode: Decisions rot if not linked to code and revisited.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.summary: Agent executor with skills, tools and sessions.
tools.why: Reads AGENTS.md and `.opencode/skills`; the installer links the canonical `.agents/skills` there.
tools.failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; its permissions must be configured, not assumed.

tools.name: Codex CLI
tools.summary: Agent executor and AGENTS.md reader.
tools.why: Discovers repository policy through AGENTS.md; the CLI remains the same portable entrypoint.
tools.failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; sandbox and approval settings vary by environment.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.summary: Agent executor with project skills.
tools.why: Reads `.claude/skills`; the installer links the canonical skill directory there.
tools.failure_mode: Executor behaviour changes between versions; permission modes must be set deliberately.

tools.name: Autobot
tools.summary: Local-first agent with threads, approvals and receipts.
tools.why: The control-plane target: one worktree per thread, durable approvals, signed gateway receipts. Not the default executor for this kit.
tools.failure_mode: Local agent in development; receipts are only as complete as the instrumentation.

tools.name: Invincible gateway
tools.summary: Model gateway with policy, redaction, receipts and audit.
tools.why: The agent should receive a gateway token, not provider keys. Keep it loopback/private and inject credentials at runtime.
tools.failure_mode: Gateway in development; a misconfigured policy can pass or block more than intended.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.summary: Self-hosted model routing and budgets.
tools.why: Centralizes provider keys and model policy. Requires the platform environment and budget configuration.
tools.failure_mode: Another service to run and secure; routing errors can send data to the wrong provider.

tools.name: GitHub
tools.summary: Issues, PRs, CI runs, artifacts and checks.
tools.why: The shared collaboration and enforcement surface. Use least-privilege tokens; never commit them.
tools.failure_mode: Platform outages and rate limits; API tokens are high-value credentials.

tools.name: Plane
tools.summary: Work items, projects and delivery tracking.
tools.why: Use when the repository's policy requires the work item to track the change. It does not authorize code changes.
tools.failure_mode: Tracking drifts from reality unless items are updated when work lands.

tools.name: pen.dev / Pencil
tools.summary: Design files and rendered UI artifacts.
tools.why: Use for UI design work when the task is visual. It does not replace code, tests or accessibility review.
tools.failure_mode: Design files drift from shipped UI without a review step.

tools.name: cargo-nextest
tools.summary: Faster Rust test runner: per-test processes, retries reported, JUnit output.
tools.why: Usually faster than cargo test on large workspaces. Does not run doctests; keep `cargo test --doc` in the gate.
tools.failure_mode: Skips doctests unless run separately; retries can hide flakes if they are treated as passes.

tools.name: mold or lld
tools.summary: A faster linker for large Rust binaries.
tools.why: Linking often dominates incremental Rust builds. Measure with and without; mold is Linux-focused, lld is cross-platform.
tools.failure_mode: Platform-specific flags; a linker difference can surface as an obscure link error or a different binary layout.

tools.name: cargo-hakari
tools.summary: Workspace-hack crate so feature unification stops causing rebuilds.
tools.why: Helps large workspaces whose crates rebuild because features differ between builds. Adds a generated crate to maintain.
tools.command: cargo hakari generate && cargo hakari verify
tools.failure_mode: A stale workspace-hack causes surprising rebuilds or feature changes; it must be verified in CI.

tools.name: cargo-chef
tools.summary: Caches Rust dependency builds as a container layer.
tools.why: Useful when CI builds in Docker and dependency compilation dominates. Not needed with a working compiler cache.
tools.command: cargo chef prepare --recipe-path recipe.json && cargo chef cook --release --recipe-path recipe.json
tools.failure_mode: Only helps container builds; a recipe out of sync with the lockfile caches the wrong dependencies.

tools.name: bacon
tools.summary: Background checker for the local Rust inner loop.
tools.why: Keeps check/clippy/test feedback running while editing. A developer convenience, not evidence: results are not recorded.
tools.failure_mode: Its output is not evidence; a green bacon pane is not a verified gate.

tools.name: cargo-deny
tools.summary: Licence, advisory, source and duplicate-version checks for Rust dependencies.
tools.why: Belongs in the required gate of Rust repositories with a reviewed deny.toml. Exceptions are narrow and dated.
tools.failure_mode: A permissive deny.toml or broad exceptions make it pass without checking; needs the advisory database (network).

tools.name: cargo-audit
tools.summary: RustSec advisory scan of Cargo.lock.
tools.why: Overlaps with cargo-deny advisories and OSV; use one consistently and keep it in the required gate.
tools.failure_mode: Advisories lag disclosure; ignored IDs must carry a reason and an expiry.

tools.name: cargo-machete
tools.summary: Finds unused dependencies in Cargo.toml.
tools.why: Fast and dependency-free; unused dependencies cost build time and attack surface.
tools.failure_mode: Text-based: false positives for dependencies used only through macros or build scripts.

tools.name: cargo-llvm-cov
tools.summary: Source-based code coverage for Rust tests.
tools.why: Shows untested code paths in a change. Coverage is a map of what ran, not a quality score.
tools.failure_mode: High coverage with weak assertions proves little; instrumented builds are slower and can change timing.

tools.name: Nix / devenv
tools.summary: Declarative, pinned development and CI environments.
tools.why: Makes 'works on my machine' reproducible across agents and runners. Steep learning curve; adopt when environment drift is a measured problem.
tools.failure_mode: Complexity and evaluation time; macOS support differs from Linux.

tools.name: mise
tools.summary: Pinned tool versions per repository (toolchains, CLIs).
tools.why: Lighter than Nix for pinning tool versions; does not pin system libraries.
tools.failure_mode: Pins tools, not the OS or system libraries; plugins fetch from the network.

tools.name: Dagger
tools.summary: CI pipelines as code that run the same locally and in CI.
tools.why: Useful when pipelines must run identically on laptops, agents and CI. Adds an engine to run and secure.
tools.failure_mode: Another runtime in the trust path; engine caching needs the same poisoning care as build caches.

tools.name: gVisor
tools.summary: User-space kernel sandbox for containers running untrusted work.
tools.why: Stronger isolation than a plain container for agent tasks on untrusted code.
tools.failure_mode: Syscall compatibility gaps and performance overhead for I/O-heavy builds.

tools.name: Firecracker
tools.summary: MicroVMs for strong per-task isolation.
tools.why: VM-level isolation with fast start-up; suits running many untrusted agent tasks on one host.
tools.failure_mode: Linux/KVM only; image, network and storage plumbing is yours to build and secure.

tools.name: Buck2 or Bazel (remote execution)
tools.summary: Hermetic builds with remote caching and execution.
tools.why: Only worth it at a scale where Cargo plus a compiler cache is measurably not enough. Large migration cost.
tools.failure_mode: Migration cost and a second build definition that can drift from Cargo; hermeticity breaks quietly.

tools.name: Temporal
tools.summary: Durable workflows for long-running, retryable agent orchestration.
tools.why: Consider when agent pipelines need durable retries and state across failures. A service to operate.
tools.failure_mode: A stateful service to run, secure and upgrade; workflow code has determinism rules that are easy to break.

tools.name: Langfuse-style agent traces
tools.summary: Traces of agent runs: prompts, tool calls, cost and latency.
tools.why: Helps find stalled or expensive agents. Traces contain prompts and code; treat them as confidential.
tools.failure_mode: Traces can capture secrets and private code; another data store to secure and retain correctly.

tools.name: Prometheus / Grafana
tools.summary: Metrics and dashboards for CI duration, queue depth, cache hit rate and cost.
tools.why: Adopt when the improvement loop needs trends that evidence files alone do not show.
tools.failure_mode: Dashboards nobody reads; metrics without definitions drift from references/metrics.md.

tools.name: Push notifications for exceptions
tools.summary: Deliver the exception digest to the human who owns it.
tools.why: Attention is scarce: push only `eng digest` items, never every pass.
tools.failure_mode: Alert fatigue if it sends passes; silent failure if the notifier breaks, so a missing digest must itself be noticed.

tools.name: KiCad with KiBot
tools.summary: Schematic/PCB design with scripted ERC/DRC and fabrication outputs.
tools.why: Makes hardware design checks reproducible in CI. Not exercised in any WCKD repository with recorded evidence.
tools.failure_mode: Rule checks only cover the rules configured; generated outputs must not be hand-edited.

tools.name: ngspice
tools.summary: Circuit simulation (SPICE).
tools.why: Checks power, sensing and driver circuits before fabrication. Results are only as good as the device models.
tools.failure_mode: Wrong or idealised models give confident wrong answers.

tools.name: Renode / QEMU
tools.summary: Emulate microcontrollers and boards to test firmware without devices.
tools.why: Runs firmware tests in CI before a bench. Peripheral models are incomplete.
tools.failure_mode: Missing or inaccurate peripheral models; timing differs from hardware.

tools.name: MuJoCo
tools.summary: Physics simulation for robot controllers.
tools.why: Tests gaits and controllers in simulation with fixed seeds before hardware.
tools.failure_mode: Sim-to-real gap: contact, friction and actuator models differ from the robot.

tools.name: Hardware-in-the-loop runner
tools.summary: A self-hosted runner attached to real devices for bench tests.
tools.why: The last step after simulation and emulation. Needs safe test sequences and human approval for anything that can damage hardware.
tools.failure_mode: Untrusted code on a runner with physical devices; flaky hardware reported as passing.

paths.title: Onboard a repository
paths.summary: Discover the map, commands and policy before touching code.
paths.when: A new repository, a stale summary, or an unfamiliar module.

steps.title: Read the policy
steps.body: Read AGENTS.md first, then the build manifests and the pull-request workflow.
steps.done: Commands are sourced from the repository, not invented.

steps.title: Build the map
steps.body: Inventory stacks, modules, tests, CI and interface candidates with the dependency-free detector.
steps.done: The map cites paths and marks its inferences.

steps.title: Install the controls
steps.body: If the repository has no `.agents/engineering.json`, install the kit and commit the resulting files.
steps.done: The config and AGENTS section are reviewed; hooks are enabled locally.

steps.title: Run the baseline
steps.body: Run the fast gate before editing and record pre-existing failures separately.
steps.done: A baseline evidence record exists and failures are known.

paths.title: Fix a bug
paths.summary: Reproduce, prove the cause, fix it, and leave a red-then-green test.
paths.when: A failing test, crash, incident or reported behavior.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.body: Capture the exact command, revision, environment and full failure. Reduce the input while it still fails.
steps.done: The smallest failing reproduction is recorded.

steps.title: Establish the baseline
steps.body: Run the existing suite and record pre-existing failures. Do not attribute them to the fix.
steps.done: Baseline results are saved.

steps.title: Write the regression test
steps.body: Add the test to the existing file for the area. Prove it fails on the unfixed revision for the reported reason.
steps.done: The test fails before the fix with the expected assertion.

steps.title: Fix the cause
steps.body: Make the smallest change that removes the cause, not the symptom. Do not combine it with a refactor.
steps.done: The reproduction and the new test pass.

steps.title: Verify and report
steps.body: Run the targeted test, the fast gate and the required full gate. Report the evidence id and residual risk.
steps.done: Evidence is pass or an explicit blocked/skip is reported.

paths.title: Add a feature
paths.summary: Turn an outcome into the smallest change with a testable contract.
paths.when: A new user-visible capability, command, endpoint or setting.

steps.title: Define the acceptance criteria
steps.body: Write what the user can observe, including defaults, errors and compatibility. Separate must-haves from preferences.
steps.done: Criteria are testable and the affected consumers are listed.

steps.title: Design the smallest interface
steps.body: Prefer an existing pattern to a new abstraction. Name the contract and its owner.
steps.done: The interface and compatibility decision are explicit.

steps.title: Implement with tests
steps.body: Add unit tests for the new behavior and integration tests at the real boundary. Keep unrelated refactors out.
steps.done: The new tests fail without the change and pass with it.

steps.title: Check the contract and security
steps.body: Add old/new fixtures for serialization, CLI output or schema changes. Run the relevant scanners.
steps.done: Compatibility and security checks are recorded.

steps.title: Ship with evidence
steps.body: Report the behavior, commands, skips and residual risk. Link the evidence record.
steps.done: A reviewer can reproduce the verification.

paths.title: Refactor safely
paths.summary: Change structure without changing observable behavior.
paths.when: Extracting modules, renaming internals, removing duplication or preparing for a feature.

steps.title: Freeze the behavior
steps.body: Run the relevant tests and add characterization or golden coverage where it is thin.
steps.done: The baseline is green or known failures are documented.

steps.title: Identify the contract
steps.body: List public symbols, serialized output, errors, defaults and performance that must not change.
steps.done: The observable surface is named.

steps.title: Move in small steps
steps.body: One mechanical step at a time. Run the compiler and narrow tests after each step.
steps.done: Each step is reviewable and green.

steps.title: Compare behavior
steps.body: Run the contract and characterization fixtures. Compare performance on hot paths.
steps.done: Outputs are identical; any change is explicit.

steps.title: Separate the discovery
steps.body: If the refactor reveals a bug, record it and open a separate change. Do not silently expand scope.
steps.done: New issues have their own evidence and owner.

paths.title: Harden a surface
paths.summary: Model the trust boundary, scan it, fix the cause, and prove the fix.
paths.when: Input parsing, auth, secrets, subprocesses, files, network, CI permissions or a scanner finding.

steps.title: Map the trust boundary
steps.body: Name the assets, actors, entry points, privileged operations and attacker-controlled data.
steps.done: The boundary and preconditions are explicit.

steps.title: Run the scanners
steps.body: Run secrets, SAST, dependency, workflow and pin checks. Read the findings, not only the counts.
steps.done: Every finding has a location and a decision.

steps.title: Fix or suppress narrowly
steps.body: Fix the cause. A false positive gets an exact, reviewed suppression with a reason; never broaden the rule.
steps.done: The scanner is clean or the exception is justified.

steps.title: Add a regression test
steps.body: Test the exploit precondition and the rejection. Do not publish exploit details in a public issue.
steps.done: The test fails on the vulnerable revision and passes after.

paths.title: Improve performance
paths.summary: Baseline, profile, change one thing, and measure the distribution.
paths.when: Latency, throughput, memory, startup or build-time work.

steps.title: Define the metric
steps.body: Choose the user-facing metric and a target. Pin the workload, hardware and build profile.
steps.done: The measurement is repeatable.

steps.title: Record the baseline
steps.body: Take at least five samples after warm-up. Keep the raw results and environment.
steps.done: Median, p95 and variance are recorded.

steps.title: Profile before changing
steps.body: Find the dominant cost. A small function is not the bottleneck just because it looks slow.
steps.done: The bottleneck has evidence.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.body: Re-run the identical workload and check correctness and other metrics.
steps.done: The effect exceeds noise and correctness holds.

paths.title: Parallelize work
paths.summary: Split by independently verifiable units, isolate them, integrate sequentially.
paths.when: Multiple independent fixes, research beside implementation, or a large feature.

steps.title: Define units
steps.body: Each unit needs an outcome, owned files, a verification command and a dependency list.
steps.done: Units do not share writable files or state.

steps.title: Create worktrees
steps.body: One worktree and branch per unit, with an owner. The CLI refuses a dirty tree and enforces the cap.
steps.done: Ownership and scope are recorded.

steps.title: Run and verify
steps.body: Implement in isolation. Each owner runs its unit's checks and records evidence.
steps.done: Each unit has isolated evidence.

steps.title: Integrate sequentially
steps.body: Rebase one unit at a time, resolve conflicts explicitly, and re-run the full gate on the latest target.
steps.done: The integrated revision passes, not just the union of unit tests.

steps.title: Clean up
steps.body: Remove merged worktrees; keep unmerged branches with a reason. Never force-remove dirty work.
steps.done: No orphaned work or shared-state corruption.

paths.title: Prepare a release
paths.summary: Bind a clean revision, passing evidence, version, notes, rollback and artifact digest.
paths.when: A tag, package, binary, container, deployment or store submission.

steps.title: Freeze the candidate
steps.body: Record the exact commit and artifact. Never release from an unverified dirty tree.
steps.done: The candidate digest is recorded.

steps.title: Run the full gate
steps.body: Run the full profile and confirm the evidence record is for this HEAD.
steps.done: The full evidence is pass for the candidate.

steps.title: Check the release contract
steps.body: Check version, changelog, notes, migration and rollback. Verify the artifact hash and any supplied signature/SBOM.
steps.done: The release record is written and reproducible.

steps.title: Get approval and publish
steps.body: Obtain explicit human approval. Publish through the approved channel. Verify the public artifact and smoke-test it.
steps.done: The published digest matches the candidate; rollback is ready.

paths.title: Run many agents in parallel safely
paths.summary: Many agents on many repositories: one task, one worktree, one sandbox, one PR, and a queue instead of collisions.
paths.when: Several agents or sub-agents work at once, share a build machine, or target the same branch.

steps.title: Write the ownership table
steps.body: List each task with its owner, owned paths, verification command and dependencies. No path has two owners; shared files go to one integration owner.
steps.done: A table with no overlapping owned paths is recorded in the work item.

steps.title: Set machine limits
steps.body: Cap concurrent worktrees and build jobs so extra work queues instead of contending. Isolate each task in its own sandbox with scoped, short-lived credentials.
steps.done: The cap, the sandbox definition and the token scopes are written down.

steps.title: Start one worktree per task
steps.body: Each agent gets its own worktree, branch, scope, budget, stop conditions and handoff format.
steps.done: Every running agent maps to exactly one worktree with an owner record.

steps.title: Verify each task on its own
steps.body: Baseline, implement, run the fast gate, then the full gate with the builder and an independent verifier recorded.
steps.done: Each task has full evidence on its own head, verified by a different identity.

steps.title: Land through the queue
steps.body: Merge one change at a time through the merge queue or auto-merge with required checks. Update dependent branches and re-run their gate after each merge.
steps.done: Main stays green; each merged revision has passing gate evidence.

steps.title: Watch by exception
steps.body: Read the digest instead of every run. Clean up finished worktrees.
steps.done: The digest is empty or every item has an owner and a next step.

paths.title: Make a Rust CI fast without lowering the gate
paths.summary: Measure, then cache, link, test and scope smarter — with before/after numbers and the same required checks.
paths.when: Rust builds or CI runs are the bottleneck for agents or reviewers.

steps.title: Baseline
steps.body: Time cold and warm builds and the CI run, per crate and per step, with enough runs to see variance. Record the list of required checks.
steps.done: Before numbers, machine, toolchain and the required-check list are recorded.

steps.title: Add a shared compiler cache
steps.body: Use a compiler cache on S3-compatible storage. Only main-branch CI writes; PR builds and agents read. Separate prefixes per project and toolchain; fixed workdir and path remapping; incremental compilation off in CI.
steps.done: Cache hit rate is recorded in evidence; write credentials exist only in main-branch CI.

steps.title: Faster linker and test runner
steps.body: Try one at a time: a faster linker (mold or lld), then cargo-nextest. Measure each separately.
steps.done: Each change has its own before/after numbers; the test set is unchanged.

steps.title: Scope tests to the change
steps.body: Use the impact list for the fast profile; keep the full suite in the merge gate and heavy suites in nightly.
steps.done: The fast profile states its scope; the full gate still runs everything it ran before.

steps.title: Keep or revert
steps.body: Compare after with before under the same conditions. Keep only changes that are faster with the same checks.
steps.done: Kept changes carry their numbers; anything slower or narrower is reverted.

paths.title: Promote a repository to autopilot
paths.summary: Reduce supervision one tier at a time, one repository at a time, on a week of evidence.
paths.when: Someone proposes letting agents merge or run a repository without per-change review.

steps.title: Check the controls
steps.body: Reproducible environment, passing full profile, tiered CI, merge queue, rollback path, spend cap, alerting, independent verification and a named human. Each needs a link or a command result.
steps.done: A checklist with evidence for every item is in the repository's work item.

steps.title: Rehearse the rollback
steps.body: Revert a harmless change (or redeploy the previous version) and confirm the system returns to the previous state.
steps.done: The rollback was exercised and its evidence is linked.

steps.title: Turn on the digest
steps.body: Deliver `eng digest` daily to the named human and set the budget cap.
steps.done: The human receives the digest and every item has an owner.

steps.title: Promote one tier
steps.body: The owner promotes the repository one tier. Other repositories wait.
commands: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets  # confirm required checks and the merge queue
steps.done: The tier decision and date are recorded by the owner.

steps.title: Hold for a week
steps.body: Collect a week of evidence: merges, digest items, reverts and cost. Demote on a failed rollback, an unexplained revert, an overspend or an ignored digest item.
steps.done: A week of evidence shows the tier holds before the next repository is considered.

paths.title: Hardware-in-the-loop (candidate)
paths.summary: Candidate path, not yet exercised: schematics, simulation and a device bench behind the same evidence standard.
paths.when: A project has electronics, firmware or a robot whose behaviour software tests cannot cover.

steps.title: Check the design files
steps.body: Run electrical and design-rule checks and generate fabrication outputs reproducibly from the source files.
steps.done: ERC/DRC results and generated outputs are attached to evidence; nothing is hand-edited.

steps.title: Simulate the circuit
steps.body: Simulate the circuits that matter (power, sensing, drivers) with stated models and limits.
steps.done: Simulation results and the model assumptions are recorded.

steps.title: Emulate the firmware
steps.body: Run firmware tests on an emulator before touching a device.
steps.done: Firmware tests pass in emulation with recorded evidence.

steps.title: Simulate the mechanism
steps.body: For robots, run the controller against a physics simulation with fixed seeds.
steps.done: Simulated runs pass with seeds and tolerances recorded.

steps.title: Run on the bench
steps.body: A self-hosted runner attached to real hardware runs a short, safe test sequence behind a human-approved gate.
steps.done: Bench results are in nightly evidence; a human approved any test that can damage hardware.

repos.name: your repository
repos.evidence: No baseline until you run it
repos.notes: Install the kit, keep AGENTS.md authoritative, and start with the fast profile. Do not copy another repository's commands without checking its build files.

limits: Impact analysis is textual, not a build graph.
The kit scans tracked files for secrets; history scanning is opt-in and untracked files are not covered until staged.
OSV needs network and a supported lockfile; no package sources means skipped, not pass.
A green gate describes only the checks that ran; it is not a proof of correctness or security.
Repository statuses are recorded observations, not live CI. Dates and evidence links are author-supplied; the portal does not fetch or verify them.
macOS and Linux are supported; the evidence index uses fcntl and does not run on Windows.
Only the pilot and local review branches have been exercised; other repositories are not yet rolled out.
The agent evaluation harness is a smoke test with two tasks, not a statistical model benchmark.
Evidence is hash-chained locally but not signed; CI artifact retention is the external trust anchor.
Builder and verifier identities in evidence are declared by the caller, not authenticated.
Quarantine is declarative: the repository's test command must exclude the test; the kit reports it as unverified and blocks on expiry.
eng digest reads local evidence, quarantine files and worktrees; it does not fetch CI artifacts, forge state or provider spend.
The delivery metrics are defined in references/metrics.md; the kit records inputs but does not compute them.
Machine-level concurrency caps are guidance; the kit enforces only parallel.max_worktrees per repository.

The build-speed, quality-gate, reproducibility, isolation, scale, observability and hardware tools are conditional or candidate; none has been exercised in this repository with recorded evidence or at fleet scale.
No repository has been promoted with the autopilot-readiness checklist yet; the hardware-in-the-loop path is a candidate.
The kit does not generate SBOMs or signatures; release-check can record and verify supplied material.
